template.description: Reproducible workbench for finding, running, benchmarking, and publishing local LLM recipes — one checkout per machine
stages: Preflight: Confirms AC power, a quiet GPU, and `LAB_MEM_CAP_GIB` from `mise run init`.
Gates (`scripts/gates.py`): Seven pass/fail checks (`load`, `chat`, `reasoning`, `tools` round-trip, `context` needle at ~85% of window, `speed`, and optional `vision`).

Baseline (`mise run bench`): Measures median single-stream decode (`c1_decode` across 6 fixed 512-token prompts), cold `4K`/`32K` prefill, verified `3/3` long-context needle retrieval, and peak physical RAM.
Ceilings (`mise run ceiling`): Derives memory-bandwidth and FLOP limits from measured hardware probes.
Hill-climb & Stability (`mise run ab`): Interleaved `ctl-a cand ctl-b` comparisons and full-context checks before promoting `best-config.json`.
template.startCommands:
mise trust && mise run init       # detect hardware with whichllm, set memory cap, update README.md
mise run hardware                 # print what whichllm detects here
mise run find                     # rank models for this machine
mise run new -- <slug>            # create models/<slug>/ for one of them
mise run serve -- start           # start DEFAULT_MODEL (or MODEL=<slug> mise run serve -- start)
mise run chat                     # start the local HTML/JS chat client on http://127.0.0.1:8088/
mise run report                   # generate SVG benchmark charts in docs/charts/

upstreamProjects.name: inference-optimisation-skill
upstreamProjects.purpose: The tuning method and benchmark scripts. Copied into `.claude/skills/inference-optimisation/`; `UPSTREAM` there records the commit, and `mise run skill-update` refreshes it.

upstreamProjects.name: whichllm
upstreamProjects.purpose: Detects this machine and ranks models for it. `mise run hardware` prints the detection; `mise run find` ranks. Nothing is copied in.

upstreamProjects.name: local-ai-registry
upstreamProjects.purpose: Published recipes to start from. `mise run registry` clones it into `.registry/`, which git ignores.

machines.label: Apple M4 Max (64 GB Unified)
machines.description: Apple M4 Max (64 GB) local LLM benchmarks & reproducible recipes: Inkling-2-Mini (80.6 tok/s), Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B (39.5 tok/s), Qwen3.8-27B (32.5 tok/s)

specs.gpu: Apple M4 Max — 48.0 GB shared (546 GB/s spec)

recipes.recipeSummary: Default fastest model (`mise run serve -- start`): 80.6 tok/s decode, 61.6 tok/s @ 30.5K, `24.9 GiB` peak
Fastest lossless Inkling: 64.2 tok/s decode without 4-bit dense/output quantization (`28.7 GiB` peak)
Zero-build convenience if running via Ollama CLI; fast at `65.4 tok/s` short with `reasoning_effort: "none"` (note long retrieval failed `0/3` with effort none)
Fastest dense 27B & agentic tool calling: 39.5 tok/s short & 39.4 tok/s @ 10.8K, `21.4 GiB` peak
Clean reference Python/MLX stack with upstream checkpoint: 34.0 tok/s decode, `24.1 GiB` peak
Lowest-RAM 27B & ultra-long 4-bit KV: 32.5 tok/s decode, 16.4 GiB peak, previously tested to `157K` @ `20.9 GiB`

footnotes: * Ollama hit 65.4 tok/s with `reasoning_effort: "none"` (`long` `0/3`) vs 28.6 tok/s with thinking on (`long` `3/3`); `mtplx` runs have thinking on; `mlx-vlm` and `llama.cpp` runs disable thinking.

† Prior `base` (`434a1bed`) also passed `3/3 @ 30.5K` (`20.4 tok/s`, `24.4 GiB`); `mtplx` 2.13.2 was also benchmarked (`61.1` / `60.0` short decode, `78.4` / `41.4` 16K decode). Full details in each `models/<slug>/PLAN.md`.
keyFindings: Fastest overall — inkling-2-mini-mtplx-bare-speed: `mtplx` `2.13.1` with 4-bit dense/unembed + L20–23 weights (`Youssofal/Inkling-2-Mini-MTPLX-Bare-Speed`) and adaptive DSpark reached 80.6 tok/s short decode (`81.1 tok/s` speed gate @ `0.433` acceptance), 721 / 700 tok/s prefill, 3/3 @ 30.5K (`61.6 tok/s`), and 24.9 GiB peak RAM (`-3.8 GiB` vs lossless quality). This is the default server launched by `mise run serve`.

Lossless Inkling — inkling-2-mini-mtplx-quality: Native NVFP4/MXFP8 weights on `mtplx` `2.13.1` reached 64.2 tok/s decode (`84%` of the 4K no-draft bandwidth ceiling) and 3/3 @ 30.5K (`43.1 tok/s`) at 28.7 GiB. Upgrading to `mtplx` `2.13.2` boosted 16K long-context decode on both packs (`78.4` and `41.4 tok/s`) while regressing short-context `c1_decode` (`61.1` and `60.0 tok/s`), so `best-config.json` remains on `2.13.1`.

Inkling on `mlx-vlm` — inkling-2-mini-mlx-nvfp4: Upgrading to `mlx-vlm` `36565bc1` (PR #2798 grouped-expert matvec) lifted decode from `33.0` → 34.0 tok/s short and `27.3` → 31.3 tok/s @ 12.8K (`24.1 GiB` peak). Pure autoregressive decode beat DSpark (`7.4` @ block 8, `28.6` @ block 2, `29.5` adaptive) because multi-token verification widens top-8/128 MoE expert union faster than acceptance amortizes.

Inkling on Ollama — inkling-2-mini-ollama: Reached 65.4 tok/s with `reasoning_effort: "none"` (but failed `0/3` on 12.8K retrieval with empty SSE chunks) vs 28.6 tok/s with thinking on (`3/3` retrieval, `28.0 GiB`).

Ternary 27B vs 4-bit 27B — bonsai-2.5-27b-llamacpp vs qwen3.8-27b-mlx-4bit: PrismML's rotated `PQ2_0-mtp` Ternary Bonsai 2.5 (`7.0 GiB` + `600M` vision projector, `87.1%` MTP acceptance) reached 39.5 tok/s decode and held 39.4 tok/s @ 10.8K (`3/3` retrieval, `21.4 GiB`, `2.0 s` startup) — beating upgraded `qwen3.8-27b-mlx-4bit` (`mlx 0.32.4` / `mlx-vlm 0.8.0`: 32.5 tok/s decode, `206 / 171` prefill, `16.4 GiB`, `157K` prior context ceiling).

macOS memory cap (scripts/init-box): Updated Darwin unified-memory capping to derive from Apple Silicon's Metal wired limit (`48 GiB - 4 GiB = 44 GiB`) rather than idle-free `vm_stat` pages (`29–32 GiB`), since macOS compresses and swaps idle desktop pages.

machines.label: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (122.8 GB Unified)
machines.description: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (122.8 GB unified) local LLM benchmarks and reproducible recipes: Inkling-2-Mini (43.0 tok/s exact, 50.0 lossy), Qwen3.8-27B (35.0 tok/s), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (17.4 tok/s)

specs.gpu: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (compute capability 11.0, `sm_110`), memory shared with the CPU; measured 256 GB/s read bandwidth and 110 TFLOPS BF16
specs.cpu: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor Developer Kit (14 cores, aarch64)
specs.note: Written by hand from measurements on the machine: the pinned `whichllm` does not detect this GPU yet (it reports CPU-only).

recipes.recipeSummary: Fastest here: 43.0 tok/s, bit-identical to the no-draft server. The default for `mise run serve`
Same decode (34.6), prefill 2.6× faster than INT4
Works, including vision; slower than vLLM (29.2)
Small footprint (28 GiB); prefill too slow for long context
The run-time LoRA costs about a third of decode speed
The largest model tried here; 17.4 tok/s
Runs; slower than vLLM on every metric
Slower decode than its sibling; stopped at baseline

footnotes: Bold is the best config of each recipe. Where two numbers are shown (`a / b*`), the recipe has no chosen best: `a` is its fastest clean run and `b` its plain baseline.

Long Retrieval is one request with a document of that many tokens and three needles. Its decode figure is a single request and is not repeatable: the same Inkling config gave 37.5, 21.1 and 42.6 tok/s on three runs.
No recipe is `qualified`. Stage 5 (documents at 50% and 100% of the window, and a soak) has not been run on any of them.

Inkling has a faster lossy variant that is not in the table: 50.0 tok/s single stream and 85.3 with four streams (`spec-dspark7-prob-avplan1-topk64-vocab-w8`, int8 copies of the BF16 decode weights). It passes the gates and scored 127 of 130 on a small exact-answer quiz against 129 for the exact config, but its output is not the checkpoint's output.
`deepseek-v4-flash-0731-exl3-3.0bpw-vllm` has no row: its engine image is built for DGX Spark (`sm_120`) and cannot run on this GPU.
`qwen3.8-27b-awq-int4-vllm`'s weights were deleted after it was superseded by `qwen3.8-27b-awq-int4-full-vllm`; the recipe remains.
keyFindings: Inkling 2 Mini on vLLM went from 33.8 to 43.0 tok/s with no change in output. Three changes did it: adaptive verification (after fixing a rounding-order difference in the attention split plan that made it look wrong), restricting the draft's recurrent correction to the top 64 candidates, and a 46,788-token draft vocabulary.
Decode here is bound by memory bandwidth. A no-draft Inkling token reads 5.65 GB and takes 30.2 ms against a 22.0 ms floor at 256 GB/s. The big kernels already run at 75–83% of bandwidth.
Halving the bytes of the BF16 weights buys 17%. Int8 copies read by a modified decode kernel give 50.0 tok/s. This is a quality trade and is labelled as one.
Fewer loop passes is not an option for Inkling. Two passes instead of the trained three is fast and produces repetitive garbage.
Recipes built for DGX Spark do not transfer by default. This GPU is `sm_110`; Spark images carry kernels compiled only for `sm_120`.
For Qwen3.8-27B, NVFP4 and AWQ INT4 decode at the same speed (about 35 tok/s with a DFlash draft), but NVFP4 prefills 2.6× faster.

Greedy output is not batch-invariant on the Inkling engine. The same prompt at temperature 0 gives different text when batched with other requests, with or without a draft, so "lossless" can only be shown single-stream.
